shapiro_wilk.note: Evaluated on N=5000 subsample per statistical standards

trend.practical_note: Slope statistically significant (p=0.000) but total drift over the window is only -0.65C — practically small.

dependence.interpretation: Extreme days show severe serial clustering (lag-1 autocorrelation=0.97, longest run=95 consecutive days, mean run=10.4 days). Crucially, P(Hot tomorrow | Hot today) = 90.4%, versus just 2.8% if today is cool. Over 97.6% of extreme days occur as part of multi-day heatwaves, proving extreme heat is persistent, not isolated.

dataset_info.underlying_model: ECMWF ERA5 Reanalysis (0.25 deg grid resolution)
dataset_info.citation: Open-Meteo.com Historical Weather Archive API (ERA5 Reanalysis by ECMWF). Data retrieved for New Delhi, India (28.6139 N, 77.209 E) spanning 1950-01-01 to 2026-10-07.
dataset_info.description: National Capital Region experiencing intense Urban Heat Island (UHI) dynamics and extreme summer heatwaves.
